passage:
Monday: Madhav and Shankar walked home the long way, past the tailor's shop, and made up a secret knock: two quick, one slow. At Shankar's gate Madhav said, "You're my best friend, okay? Only mine." Shankar grinned and did the knock on his school bag.
Thursday: At recess Shankar ran off to play marbles with the new boy, Arif. Madhav stood by the tap pretending to drink water for a long time. When Shankar waved, he didn't do the knock.
Saturday: Madhav's Appa asked why he was sulking. "He played with Arif," Madhav muttered. Appa said friends can have other friends and still come back. On the way to the shop they saw Shankar, who did two quick, one slow on a lamppost. Madhav hesitated, then knocked back.

qa.a: The secret knock was two quick, one slow.

qa.q: What was Madhav feeling as he stood by the tap at recess?
qa.a: Madhav felt hurt and left out; pretending to drink water was a way to hide it when Shankar ran to Arif. 🥺

qa.q: What could help Madhav with this first hurt?
qa.a: Like Appa did, an adult can explain that playing with Arif doesn't end the friendship, and Madhav could try asking Arif to join their game too.

qa.q: How might Shankar see the recess moment?
qa.a: Shankar probably just wanted to try marbles with the new boy and may not have known it hurt Madhav, which is why he still did the knock on Saturday.

grounding: Shows two boys becoming best friends through walks home and a secret code, with the joy and possessiveness that brings the first hurt at recess.

passage:
Come, sit. You're sulking because Riddhi played with the new girl, na? Let me tell you about your Nani and Amandeep.
We were ten, in Ludhiana. Every afternoon we walked home together along the canal, and we had a code: if one of us tugged an earlobe, it meant "meet at the neem tree after tea." We scratched our initials into its bark. She said, "You are my best friend, Chandrika, forever," and I felt as if the sky belonged to me.
Then one day at recess she skipped rope with Kamaljit's group. Just once. I went home and refused dinner. I told my mother Amandeep was a traitor.
Next morning she tugged her ear at me in the assembly line, as if nothing had happened. And for her, nothing had.
It hurt, beta, and it was also a little silly. Both.

qa.q: What did Chandrika and Amandeep scratch into the neem tree?
qa.a: They scratched their initials into its bark.

qa.q: How did Chandrika feel when Amandeep skipped rope with another group?
qa.a: Chandrika felt betrayed and hurt, enough to refuse dinner and call Amandeep a traitor.

qa.q: What is Chandrika trying to teach with this memory?
qa.a: That the hurt is real, but a friend playing with others once doesn't end a friendship, so the grandchild can feel sad without deciding Riddhi is a traitor.

qa.q: How did Amandeep probably see that day at recess?
qa.a: For Amandeep it was just a game of skipping; nothing had changed, which is why she tugged her ear the next morning as usual.

grounding: Illustrates a best friendship built on walks home, a code and 'best friend forever', and the first possessive hurt when the friend plays with others at recess.
